newsitem.title: USA: Miami reporter jailed over testimony refusal.
newsitem.headline: Miami reporter jailed over testimony refusal.

text.p: A reporter for the Miami Herald was in prison on contempt of court charges on Tuesday for refusing to answer lawyers' questions about an interview with a suspected child murderer, the newspaper reported Tuesday.
Florida Circuit Judge Roger Colton in West Palm Beach Monday sentenced David Kidwell, 35, to 70 days imprisonment in the Palm Beach County Detention Centre and a $500 fine.

The dispute arose from a jailhouse interview and subsequent Miami Herald story about John Zile, who is facing a retrial on first-degree murder charges for the 1994 beating death of Christina Holt, his 7-year-old stepdaughter.

Pauline Zile, the child's mother and Zile's wife, was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life in prison for standing by as Zile allegedly beat and suffocated the girl. The couple told police the child had been kidnapped from a Fort Lauderdale flea market but police suspected a hoax and John Zile eventually led them to Christina's battered body, buried behind a local shopping centre.
Kidwell had defended his refusal to discuss the interview as a matter of principle, saying reporters should not testify about interviews they conduct or the stories they write.

Prosecutors had wanted Kidwell to verify the substance of his article, which included incriminating statements by Zile. The Herald said its attorneys and editors had fought legal battles on Kidwell's behalf but ultimately advised him to answer questions about the interview and the story.
The newspaper said it would continue to pay Kidwell's salary during his jail term and that other members of its staff had offered to pay the $500 fine.
Zile's first trial ended in a deadlocked jury in May and his retrial was set for Oct. 15.
